pr_title: Add support for multiple devices linked to a Viessmann account
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

This change enables the integration to display all supported devices from the configured Viessmann account.

⚠️ This leads to a drop in update interval when there are multiple devices as all devices share the daily API rate limit of 1500 calls.

Verified with two heatings (Vitodens 300-W) connected via two Vitoconnect 100 OPTO1 on one site.

edit: The sensors now make use of [`_attr_has_entity_name`](https://developers.home-assistant.io/blog/2022/07/10/entity_naming/). In addition the device name has been extended by the serial number to avoid name clashes when the same model is used (which is not the case in my setup).
Is anything more required from my side?

I ran into API rate limit issues yesterday (end of month), which probably happened because of the additional requests for the second device. I guess we would need to have an ability to adjust the api call rate.

issue_context.title: Home Assistant / API doesn't get data from Viessmann hybrid system
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hello,      

I have connected Home Assistant and my Viessmann hybrid system (Vitocal (heating pump) and Vitodens (gas)) via Viessmann API.     

In HomeAssistant, however, only Vitodens is recognized, even if I enter "hybrid" or "heatpump". But I need both devices or if only one works, I would need the heat pump. 

**Overall goal: I as house owner want to use my pv energy to heat up the water in the puffer/water tank.** 

What am I doing wrong? Or does the API not pass the data?      
Thanks for feedback 🙂

P.S. I created a ticket at the Viessmann dev portal too (german only) https://www.viessmann-community.com/t5/Feedback-API/Home-Assistant-API-erkennt-Hybrid-System-bzw-Waermepumpe-nicht/m-p/376282#M241

core-2023.10.5

review_comments: This uses the device type provided in the configuration. In my setup it's fine as I have two devices of the same type (gas boilers). Others could have issues when multiple devices of *different types* are present and the type cannot be determined via type `auto` by the library. Can we go with this as a limitation or is there a better way to configure the device type? Maybe this is acceptable as currently there is only support for one device?

Do you know if this code will raise any errors? We should make sure that if a user has multiple devices, where one cannot be detected, then at least all the others will be setup correctly.
Can the user do something to help detection?

No, there will be no error. 
If a device is not recognized, it will be handled as a *generic heating device*. This could later on lead to `PyViCareNotSupportedFeatureError` which are handled on platform level.
It's fine for me. Are you mentioning which device types are supported in the docs or elsewhere?

Yes, in the docs there is a list of supported types, but no detailed list.

https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/blob/c2596f56fd802a03d3a6932fac1c7bd91d493fe2/source/_integrations/vicare.markdown?plain=1#L47
